questions.q: Enlarge P(2, 3) by scale factor 2 from centre (0, 0), then from centre (1, 1).
questions.model: Centre (0, 0): double the coordinates, (4, 6). Centre (1, 1): P is 1 right and 2 up; doubled, 2 right and 4 up: (3, 5).

questions.q: A triangle has sides 3 cm, 4 cm and 5 cm. Enlarge by scale factor 2.5.
A square of side 4 cm is enlarged by scale factor 3. Its new perimeter?
Triangle T has vertices (1, 1), (3, 1) and (1, 4). Enlarge T by (a) scale factor 2, centre (0, 0) (b) scale factor 3, centre (1, 1) (c) scale factor 2, centre (2, 0). Write each image's coordinates.
questions.model: (b) (1, 1) is the centre, so it stays put. (3, 1) is 2 right of the centre: × 3 = 6 right, so (7, 1). (1, 4) is 3 up: × 3 = 9 up, so (1, 10).

questions.q: Scale factor 3: a 7 cm side becomes
Big question: what changes and what stays the same in an enlargement?
questions.a: Lengths are multiplied by the scale factor; angles and the shape stay the same.
